signals.title: JPY/NOK — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry Deficit
signals.text: The G10 currency strength scorecard registers JPY as the week's strongest performer with an average gain of +1.189% across 7 pairs, while NOK is the laggard at −0.925% across 2 pairs. This generates a 2.114% leader-to-laggard divergence, well above the 1.20% strong-theme threshold. The move decouples from standard rate logic, as Norges Bank at 4.50% holds a 325bp policy rate advantage over the Bank of Japan at 1.25%, with the JPY 10Y sovereign yield trailing US yields by 222bp. Leveraged funds hold net long JPY positions of +4,472 contracts, sitting in the 98th percentile of their 52-week historical distribution with a z-score of +2.66, reflecting crowded positioning despite recent weekly reductions. USD/NOK trades at 9.604, positioned firmly above its SMA20 at 9.390 and SMA50 at 9.427, reflecting persistent broad NOK weakness across G10 crosses. Trade bias: Bearish NOK vs JPY, following G10 cross divergence despite negative carry. Catalyst: Tokyo CPI release at 23:30 UTC. Risk: Sharp rebound in energy benchmarks or hawkish Norges Bank commentary that forces carry realignment.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew + Volatility Regime
signals.text: USD/JPY spot trades at 157.56, holding between its 20-day SMA at 156.07 and its 50-day SMA at 158.26. The 25-delta 1-month risk reversal prints an extreme put skew of −2.60, demonstrating aggressive institutional demand for downside protection despite spot holding near multi-week highs. Options implied volatility sits at 9.1% against 30-day realized volatility of 9.9%, producing a negative volatility risk premium of −0.8% that signals suppressed premium pricing relative to realized movement. The Fed at 4.00% maintains a 275bp policy rate advantage over the BoJ at 1.25%, with the overnight SOFR-to-TONA spread delivering a +265bp carry benefit to USD holders. This combination indicates the options market is heavily pricing downside tail risk while spot remains tethered to positive carry flows below technical resistance at the 158.26/158.47 SMA cluster. Trade bias: Neutral USD/JPY, balancing elevated downside put hedging against a 265bp OIS carry floor. Catalyst: Tokyo Core CPI release at 23:30 UTC. Risk: A sustained daily close above the 50-day SMA at 158.26 invalidating the options downside skew.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Rates Driver + Technical Cluster
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1330, positioned below its SMA20 at 1.1501, SMA50 at 1.1535, and SMA200 at 1.1618. Fed policy at 4.00% holds a 135bp nominal premium deposit rate at 2.65%, reinforced by an overnight SOFR-to-€STR carry advantage of +144bp favoring the dollar. US 5Y yields rose +23bp over the trailing 5 sessions (FRED, as of Sep 29), split as real yield +21bp and breakeven +2bp, confirming a real-yield-led widening. European inflation prints accelerated across Germany, France, Italy, and Spain, yet the single currency failed to sustain gains as German 10Y Bunds trail US 10Y yields by 171bp. Implied volatility runs at 5.8% against HV30 of 3.5%, registering an elevated volatility risk premium of +2.3% as participants pay up for protection beneath the descending moving-average structure. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD, constrained by US real yield expansion and negative technical alignment. Catalyst: Euro Area CPI y/y release at 09:00 UTC. Risk: An upside core inflation shock forcing the ECB to accelerate tightening and lifting spot above 1.1501.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Macro Flow + Positioning Exhaustion
signals.text: AUD/USD prints at 0.6949, remaining below its SMA20 at 0.7115, SMA50 at 0.7095, and SMA200 at 0.7030. Leveraged funds hold net long positions of +55,684 contracts (CFTC, week ending Sep 22), ranking in the 81st percentile of their 52-week range with an absolute long ratio of 74.5%. That institutional length faces headwinds following Australia manufacturing PMI dropping into contraction at 49.6 alongside falling new orders. Australia 2Y yield spreads relative to the US narrowed by 22bp over 5 sessions to +0bp, stripping away the policy divergence cushion despite the nominal RBA 4.60% vs Fed 4.00% benchmark spread. S&P Global manufacturing data softening alongside domestic dovish commentary leaves crowded speculative longs vulnerable to further liquidation toward multi-month lows. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/USD, driven by domestic growth deceleration and unwinding yield advantage. Catalyst: Australia Trade Balance at 01:30 UTC. Risk: A rebound in commodities and Chinese demand drivers pushing spot back above the 200-day SMA at 0.7030.
